message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2024) | Area | Key Rights & Protections | |------|--------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within **30 days** after lease ends, minus any lawful deductions. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a safe, livable condition (plumbing, heating, electrical, etc.).
• Tenants can withhold rent or repair and deduct if landlord fails to maintain habitability. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on rent increases, but must be in writing and given **at least 30 days’ notice** for month‑to‑month leases.
• For fixed‑term leases, rent can only change at the start of a new term unless otherwise agreed. | | **Lease Termination** | • **Month‑to‑month**: 30‑day written notice required from either party.
• **Fixed‑term**: Must follow lease terms; early termination may require a penalty or mutual agreement. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must provide a **written notice** (e.g., 3‑day notice for nonpayment, 30‑day notice for lease violation).
• Eviction must go through court; no “self‑help” evictions allowed. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering the unit, except in emergencies. | | **Discrimination** | • Protected under the **Fair Housing Act**: no discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or source of income. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If landlord fails to fix major problems, tenant may repair and deduct from rent, but must follow proper procedure and keep receipts. | | **Right to a Written Lease** | • While not required, having a written lease clarifies rights and responsibilities. | | **Security Deposit Deductions** | • Landlord may deduct for: unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear, cleaning costs, and other contractual obligations. | | **Notice of Rent Increase** | • Must be in writing and delivered at least **30 days** before the increase takes effect. | | **Subletting** | • Tenants may sublet only with landlord’s written consent, unless lease prohibits it. | | **Landlord’s Right to Inspect** | • Landlord may inspect the unit with reasonable notice, typically 24 hours, for maintenance or safety reasons. | | **Tenant’s Right to Repair** | • If landlord fails to repair, tenant may:
1. Pay for repairs and deduct from rent (after giving notice).
2. Withhold rent (after giving notice).
3. Terminate lease (after giving notice). | | **Legal Remedies** | • Tenants can file a complaint with the Texas Attorney General’s Office or local housing agency.
• Can sue for damages or seek injunctions in civil court. | #### Quick Checklist for Tenants 1. **Read Your Lease** – Understand rent amount, due dates, security deposit, pet policy, and notice periods. 2. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of all communications, receipts, and photos of any damage or maintenance issues. 3. **Give Proper Notice** – When moving out or terminating a lease, provide written notice per the lease or state law. 4. **Know Your Rights** – If you suspect unlawful eviction, discrimination, or habitability violations, consult a tenant‑rights organization or attorney. #### Resources - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division**: [https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov](https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov) - **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs**: [https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us](https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us) - **Local Legal Aid Organizations**: Many cities have free or low‑cost legal assistance for tenants. --- **Disclaimer:** This information is general in nature and not legal advice. For specific situations, consult a licensed attorney familiar with Texas landlord‑tenant law.
